questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A man presented with frequent urination and increased thirst. MRI revealed the absence of the posterior pituitary bright spot. He was initiated on desmopressin which improved his symptoms. The affected structure is derived from:
questions.explanation: The scenario of polyuria and polydipsia with absence of the posterior pituitary bright spot is suggestive of central diabetes insipidus. It involves the diencephalon, which is derived from the prosencephalon. The diencephalon forms the thalamus, epithalamus, subthalamus and hypothalamus. The source MRI identifies the posterior pituitary bright spot and distinguishes the anterior and posterior pituitary.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is false regarding the anatomical relations of the thalamus?

options.text: Anterior pole of thalamus forms the posterior boundary of the interventricular foramen
Pulvinar projects over the superior colliculus
Medial surface of thalamus forms the inferior boundary of III ventricle
The posterior limb of the internal capsule is laterally related to the thalamus

questions.correctAnswerText: Medial surface of thalamus forms the inferior boundary of III ventricle
questions.explanation: The medial surface of the thalamus forms the lateral wall, not the inferior boundary, of the third ventricle. The source gives thalamic relations: anteriorly, interventricular foramen; superiorly, stratum zonale with body of fornix and ventricle above; posteriorly, pulvinar overhanging the superior colliculus; inferiorly, the plane connecting hypothalamic sulci; medially, lateral wall of third ventricle; laterally, posterior limb of internal capsule.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The following section of the brain is given to you. Which of the following is true about the marked structure?

options.text: The external medullary lamina is a sheet of grey matter on the lateral surface of thalamus
The intralaminar nuclei lie outside the internal medullary lamina
The internal medullary lamina divides the thalamus into three parts
The internal medullary lamina divides the thalamus into two parts

questions.correctAnswerText: The internal medullary lamina divides the thalamus into three parts
questions.explanation: The marked structure X is the thalamus. The internal medullary lamina is a Y-shaped sheet of white matter dividing the thalamus into three parts: anterior, medial and lateral nuclear groups. The external medullary lamina is a sheet of white matter on the lateral surface of the thalamus and separates it from the reticular nucleus. Intralaminar nuclei lie within the internal medullary lamina, while midline nuclei lie close to the lateral walls of the third ventricle.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is false about the anterior thalamic nuclei?

options.text: Largest subdivision is the anteromedial nucleus
Receives fibers from the mamillary body
Lesion on this nuclei can cause amnesia
Involved in regulation of alertness and attention

questions.correctAnswerText: Largest subdivision is the anteromedial nucleus
questions.explanation: The largest subdivision of the anterior thalamic nuclei is the anteroventral nucleus, not the anteromedial nucleus. The anterior thalamic nuclei have anteroventral, anteromedial and anterodorsal subdivisions. Major input comes through the mammillothalamic tract from mammillary nuclei of the hypothalamus. Major cortical output is to anterior limbic area, cingulate and parahippocampal gyrus. Functions include regulation of alertness and attention and acquisition of memory.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The medial nucleus of the thalamus predominantly receives input from the ______ and sends output to the ______.
questions.explanation: The medial nucleus of the thalamus predominantly receives input from the hypothalamus and sends output to the prefrontal cortex. The medial thalamic group includes the large dorsomedial nucleus and smaller nuclei. The dorsomedial nucleus is connected internally to other thalamic nuclei and externally has major connections with prefrontal cortex and hypothalamus. Its functions include integration of somatic, visceral and olfactory sensory information and relation of this information to emotional feelings and subjective states.

questions.question: Choose the incorrect statement with respect to thalamic nuclei.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A man sustained a head injury 6 weeks back, following a road traffic accident. Now, he complains of increased frequency of urination and excessive thirst. An injury to which nucleus is likely to cause the given condition?
questions.explanation: Lesion of the supraoptic nucleus of the hypothalamus inhibits synthesis of vasopressin and can cause diabetes insipidus. The hypothalamus is part of the diencephalon below the thalamus. The source notes that anteriorly the preoptic area is included, posteriorly it merges with midbrain tegmentum, and laterally it is bounded by the internal capsule.

questions.question: What structure is not a part of the epithalamus?

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A woman with right-sided loss of sensations of both the upper and lower limb complains of shooting pain from her fingers to the right shoulder and a burning sensation when touching cold water. Motor functions are normal. Which of the following structures is likely to be involved?
questions.explanation: The clinical stem of hemisensory loss with severe excruciating/burning pain is suggestive of thalamic pain syndrome (Dejerine-Roussy syndrome). The thalamus, marked B, is most likely involved. Occlusion of thalamic and thalamogeniculate branches can produce contralateral hemisensory loss that may progress to severe burning pain during recovery from thalamic infarction. The source identifies the other marks as A: caudate nucleus; C: substantia nigra; D: pons.
